Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the required wake-visual inspection skill. I’ll use the rollout keyframes and inherited evidence to drive one candidate, then update both the candidate notes and the reusable control guidance.

The contract confirms the candidate must remain materializable throughout and that CFD is deferred. The wake skill is now governing the workflow: I’ll anchor the visual comparison to scores, trajectories, and diagnostics before touching the policy.

The sampled set is a clean direct body-rate sweep: every run still exits upward, while the strongest finite run reaches 4.87L and 0.424 progress but pays higher loads. I’m now comparing that sheet against the lower-progress failures to identify whether the remaining error is insufficient steering authority, delayed sign reversal, or simply more of the same upward loop.

The visual comparison rules out passive advection: all candidates generate strong upstream motion into the developed wake, then curl upward before reaching it. The 11° posterior bias improves closest approach by 0.46L over the 10°/0.70 anchor, but the nearly unchanged +1.79L head drift and 25% higher RMS loads falsify “keep increasing static bias” as the repair. I’m checking the inherited optimizer notes now for the cleanest phase-aware posterior alternative.

The inherited notes contain an explicit falsification branch, and the new 11° rollout lands on it exactly: better upstream approach, but no lateral correction and substantially worse force/moment. I’m recording the resulting phase-selective posterior hypothesis before changing the controller, as required by the wake skill.

The durable guidance now records the closed static-bias bracket: 8° loses propulsion; 11° buys approach with higher saturation/load but leaves the route unchanged. I’m implementing the single next mechanism on the 10°/0.70/0.35 anchor: bounded phase-selective relief in the posterior joint only.

The candidate, provenance notes, and reusable lesson are all in place. The controller keeps the upstream-capable oscillator intact and only attenuates posterior bias on reinforcing gait phases; next I’m running the non-CFD contract, schema, and workspace-boundary checks.

The guidance checker exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice, so the validator sees two parents before it can inspect our lesson. I’m removing only that duplicate metadata entry, then rerunning the required check; the parent identity and evidence remain unchanged.

All three local non-CFD checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract/finite action, and solver boundary. Per the workspace contract, I’m now invoking the dedicated check-runner for an independent final validation.
